decisionsTitle: A volunteer ticks every role they would do; the organizers give each one a role
decisionsSection:
**The owner, 2026-10-14 morning**, on the volunteers' public form (§754, §758, in production): «Când se înscrie un voluntar, poate bifa mai multe atribuțiuni din ce e dispus să facă (definite de noi), de exemplu: stă la masă, stă pe traseu, stă în punctele de alimentare etc.». The form took **one** role; a volunteer should tick every role of the event they are willing to do, and the organizers then give each volunteer the role they need them in. Amends §754 (the form, the card, the count, the emails, the CSV) and §758 (the role the agreement names).

**Decision — the data.** A table of its own, `event_volunteer_role_choices` (migration `0149`, expand only): the volunteer (`ON DELETE CASCADE`), a role of the event, the moment, the pair the primary key — the roles the person said they would do. `event_volunteers.role_id` stays and becomes the role **given** by the organizers; it accepts NULL for an offer nobody has placed yet (a relaxing change: dropping `NOT NULL` refuses nothing the code serving during the migration writes, so it is an expand). Every existing volunteer's role became both their one choice and the role given, in the same migration (`tests/integration/db/volunteer-role-choices-migration.test.ts` proves the backfill on PGlite, twice-safe). **The choice's reference to the role is `CASCADE`, not `RESTRICT`**: deleting an event cascades to its roles and to its volunteers, and a choice is reached only through the volunteers' second-level cascade — after the roles' own check — so a `RESTRICT` (or `NO ACTION`) there refused deleting every event with an offer (proven on PGlite before the change). The service still refuses deleting a role anybody was given **or ticked**, cancelled people included (`VOLUNTEER_ROLE_HAS_PEOPLE`: change their roles first), so nothing a person offered disappears under them.

**«N din M» counts the roles given, only.** An offer holds no place: the role's need is counted against the people the organizers gave it («Înscris» and «Confirmat», never «Anulat», as before), and the public form's «mai e nevoie de N» reads the same count. A role may be given to more people than it asked («3 din 2»), as a hand entry always could. §754's accepted residual — a new address on the form lowered the public count, a listed one did not — is gone with it: a sign-up no longer moves the count.

**The public form.** The role select becomes «Ce ești dispus(ă) să faci» / “What you are willing to do”: a fieldset with a glyph, one native checkbox per role that still needs people (the house's `CheckboxField`, one name `roleIds` posted once per tick, a 44-pixel row), each with its name and, under it, its description and how many it still needs. At least one is the service's rule, said in plain words in the refusal's summary and at the group («Bifează cel puțin un rol la „Ce ești dispus(ă) să faci”»); the ticks come back after a refusal through the sealed draft (one string of ids), never in the address. Works with scripts off. The consent, the agreement's and the age's ticks, the honeypot, the timing check, Turnstile and both throttles are unchanged. **A role that filled while the form was open:** the post locks the ticked roles (in the order of their ids — the order a role change locks them, so two posts ticking the same roles in opposite orders never deadlock; the two-connection suite holds it) and keeps those that still need people; the others ticked are kept; only when none is left is the offer refused politely («Rolurile bifate tocmai s-au umplut»), the roles still open listed under it — and, as before, that «full» is answered before the repeat is looked for, so it tells a listed address from a stranger by nothing. A repeat changes nothing, the choices included.

**The card «Voluntari».** A group **«De repartizat»** above the roles holds the offers with no role given, with how many wait («K de repartizat», also on the card's closed line, which opens the card by itself like «de confirmat»). Every person's row shows their choices as chips under «S-a oferit pentru» (a glyph and the role's name, never colour alone). A row under «De repartizat» that is not cancelled carries one press **«Dă-i rolul …»** per role ticked, its words saying how the role stands («Dă-i rolul Sosire · 0 din 1»), plus «Alt rol» — a native select of the event's other roles with how each stands, drawn only when there is one — and «Dă-i rolul ales». A person who already has a role carries no such press (one press would move them and email them without a word of warning): their role changes in «Modifică» → «Rolul dat». Each role's group lists the people given it, with «N din M». Giving a role is its own verb, asserted on the server for the Organizer, the Administrator and the Superadministrator (`canManageVolunteers`), audited as `volunteer.assigned` (the volunteer's id, the role's and the one before, never the person's words), refused for a role of another event (`VALIDATION_ERROR`) and for a cancelled person (`CONFLICT`: reopen first) — «Modifică» refuses a cancelled person a new role the same way; a press that changes nothing writes and sends nothing. **Every writer of a role reference locks the event's roles first, in the order of their ids** — «Dă-i rolul», a hand entry and «Modifică», as a sign-up and a role change do: before, a hand entry's foreign keys took KEY SHARE on the role given and then on each tick in the order posted, and against a sign-up locking the same roles FOR UPDATE in id order the two waited in a circle (40P01); the two-connection suite now races a hand entry and an edit naming two roles and a role given against sign-ups and a move. «Adaugă un voluntar de mână» and every «Modifică» take the ticks («Ce e dispus(ă) să facă») and, optionally, «Rolul dat» (any role of the event, or none): at least one of the two; a person entered with a role given and nothing ticked has that role as their one choice, so every row says what the person offered. Taking a role back is «Modifică» → «Încă niciunul (de repartizat)».

**Emails.** The person's «Ți-am primit oferta…» names the roles they offered for on the bold line («Te-ai oferit pentru: Masă, Traseu»; the role given instead, once there is one, since the line is read at the send) and says the organizers choose the role and write when they have given it; the organizers' notice names the person and those roles. **A new message, `VOLUNTEER_ROLE_ASSIGNED`** («Rolul tău de voluntar la …» / “Your volunteer role at …”), one short message through the outbox, in the same transaction as the change, in the person's language with both halves: the role and the event's start and place on the bold line, what the role asks when the club wrote it, nothing to press and no token; queued whenever a role is newly given — by «Dă-i rolul», by «Modifică», or with a person entered by hand —, when a role is kept while «Modifică» corrects the address (the first went to the old one), and when a cancelled person with a role is reopened (the receipt promised the message); withdrawn at the send when the role was changed again or taken back since, the person was cancelled, or the address was corrected since (only the role that stands is announced, to the address the row holds). The house sends nothing on «Confirmat», so there was no confirmation to reuse. Its group is «confirmations», its privacy line the volunteers' list's.

**The volunteer agreement (§758) — the words are the template's, never the code's.** An agreement accepted on the form names no role given, and the review refused the first draft's way of saying so: a clause typed in TypeScript («stabilit de organizatori; voluntarul este disponibil pentru: …») put into the approved sentence «… în rolul {{volunteerRole}}.» — a term the club never approved, in the stored blanks, the fingerprint and the PDF (CLAUDE.md: no legal text in effect that the club did not approve). The template now carries its own sentences: «Voluntarul ajută la evenimentul {{event}}, care are loc {{eventDate}}, în {{eventLocation}}.»; «Voluntarul are rolul {{volunteerRole}}.»; «Rolul îl stabilesc organizatorii dintre cele pentru care voluntarul s-a oferit — {{volunteerRoleChoices}} — și i-l comunică pe email.»; «Ce presupune rolul: {{volunteerTasks}}.»; «Ce presupune fiecare rol: {{volunteerChoiceTasks}}.» (English in parallel). Each role field drops its own paragraph when empty (`PARAGRAPH_MERGE_FIELDS`): a role given keeps the role and its tasks, none given keeps the roles offered for and what each asks. The values are the club's words only — the roles' names, «Masă, Traseu», and their descriptions by name, «Masă — dă numerele; Traseu — arată drumul» (`agreementRoleWords`). **Until a version from that template is in force**, the text a person reads (asked of that one version: `namesVolunteerRoleChoices`) has room for one role, and `{{volunteerRole}}` takes the chosen roles' names alone — «în rolul Masă, Traseu.» — with no word of the code's own; `/admin/tasks` carries the row `volunteerRoleChoicesAgreement` (open while an agreement is in force, an event ahead takes volunteers and the text in force does not name `{{volunteerRoleChoices}}` in every language; absent while no agreement is in force, whose own row covers it) and CLAUDE.md's item 16 says a lawyer reads the two new sentences first. Two blanks join the row's `agreement_facts` (`volunteerRoleChoices`, `volunteerChoiceTasks`); a row accepted before reads them as "". The link's page says «disponibil(ă) pentru: …» while no role is given. «Semnat pe hârtie» posts back what the printed sheet named — the role given, or the roles chosen (`agreementRolesStamp`) — and is refused (`VOLUNTEER_AGREEMENT_REPRINT`) when either changed since. The card's «Contractul acceptat numește: {roles}. Rolurile s-au schimbat de atunci.» names only the roles' names the accepted text held (`acceptedRoleNames`), and shows only when they no longer describe the person: given a role they never offered for, or their choices changed (`agreementStillNamesRole`).

**The CSV** gains «S-a oferit pentru» (the roles chosen, joined by «, », in the club's order) beside «Rolul dat» (empty while none); its rows are grouped by the role given, the offers to place first. «Toate datele unei persoane» lists every role an offer ticked beside the role given, so an access request stays complete.

**The privacy notice's template**, section 5, now says the offer keeps «rolurile pe care le-ai bifat și rolul pe care ți-l dau organizatorii» and that «când organizatorii îți dau un rol, primești un e-mail scurt care îl numește»; the marker and the switch are unchanged. Only a version the club approves has effect (§639's email tells the Administrators the template moved); a lawyer reads the paragraph with the rest.

**Not changed:** the agreement's gates and acceptance, the privacy rules (no public list of volunteers, no address in an email to the organizers or in the trail), the retention (the choices go with the offer), the event's JSON file (volunteers never travel), registrations and the capacity.

**The words the owner reads.** «E-mailuri» describes `VOLUNTEER_RECEIVED` as the receipt naming the roles offered for and saying the organizers choose the role, and its hints say «rolurile pentru care s-a oferit (sau rolul dat)» and «pentru ce roluri»; the card speaks to the organizer as «tu» like its neighbours; the «full» answer fits one tick or several («Ce ai bifat tocmai s-a umplut»).

**Refused.** Counting an offer against a role's need (a role would fill with people who were only willing, and the organizers could not choose); giving the first role ticked by itself (the organizers asked to choose); an order of preference among the ticked roles (nobody asked; the message box carries it); a `RESTRICT` on the choice's role (it refused deleting an event, above); a second form for staff (the card's verbs are the house's plain forms); a clause of the code's own in the agreement while the club's text has room for one role (above); a one-press move on a row that already has a role.

Amends §754 and §758.
changelogLine: - **Volunteers tick every role they would do** — «Ce ești dispus(ă) să faci» on the event's page takes several roles; the organizers find each offer under «De repartizat» on the «Voluntari» card, give one role with one press («Dă-i rolul …», showing how the role stands) and the person is told by a short email; «N din M» counts only the roles given; the CSV names the roles offered for. The volunteer agreement's template names the roles offered for in its own sentences — approve it again (`/admin/tasks` says so). §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Amends criterion 33. Given an event that takes volunteers, when a visitor opens «Vreau să fiu voluntar», then «Ce ești dispus(ă) să faci» offers one checkbox per role that still needs people — its name, its description and how many it still needs, 44 pixels a row, working with scripts off — and a post with none ticked is refused naming the box; a post keeps the ticked roles that still need people as the person's choices and gives the row no role; a ticked role that filled meanwhile is dropped and the others kept; only when none is left is the answer «full», in words that fit one tick or several, given before the repeat is looked for, to a listed address and a stranger alike (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criteria 120 and 121. Given the event's «Voluntari» card, then «N din M» counts only the people given each role («Înscris» and «Confirmat»), the public form reads the same count, and the offers with no role given are listed under «De repartizat» above the roles, each with its choices as chips under «S-a oferit pentru»; only such a row, not cancelled, carries one «Dă-i rolul …» per role ticked, naming how the role stands, and «Alt rol» for the event's other roles, drawn only when there is one; a person given a role changes it in «Modifică» → «Rolul dat»; giving a role is audited as `volunteer.assigned`, refused for another event's role and for a cancelled person, by «Dă-i rolul» and «Modifică» alike; a person entered by hand or changed takes the roles ticked and, optionally, the role given — at least one of the two; a role anybody was given or ticked is not deleted; the CSV carries «Rolul dat» and «S-a oferit pentru» (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a hand entry or a «Modifică» naming several roles and a role given, racing public sign-ups ticking the same roles and a role edited or moved on two connections, then every writer locks the event's roles in the order of their ids and all of them settle, none aborted by a deadlock (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Migration `0149_volunteer_role_choices` is expand-only: the message type `VOLUNTEER_ROLE_ASSIGNED`, the table `event_volunteer_role_choices` (the volunteer and the role each `ON DELETE CASCADE`, the pair the primary key) and `event_volunteers.role_id` relaxed to accept NULL; each existing volunteer's role becomes their one choice and stays the role given; an event with offers still deletes whole (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 130. «Semnat pe hârtie» is refused (`VOLUNTEER_AGREEMENT_REPRINT`) when the version in force, the role given or the roles chosen changed since the sheet was printed; the card's «Contractul acceptat numește …» names the roles' names the accepted text held and shows only when they no longer describe the person (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Amends criterion 42. Given a role newly given to a volunteer — by «Dă-i rolul …», by «Modifică» or with a person entered by hand —, a role kept while «Modifică» corrects the address, or a cancelled person with a role reopened, then one `VOLUNTEER_ROLE_ASSIGNED` is queued in the same transaction, to the address the row holds, in the person's language, naming the role, the event's start and place and what the role asks, with no token; it is withdrawn at the send when the role was changed again or taken back, the person cancelled or the address corrected since; and the person's «am primit» and the organizers' notice name the roles the person offered for, as «E-mailuri» describes them (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a volunteer agreement accepted or printed for a person, then its role blanks hold only the club's words — the roles' names and descriptions: the role given in `{{volunteerRole}}` and `{{volunteerTasks}}`; with none given, the roles chosen in `{{volunteerRoleChoices}}` and `{{volunteerChoiceTasks}}`, the template's own sentences, each paragraph left out when its field is empty — or, under a version that names no `{{volunteerRoleChoices}}`, the chosen roles' names alone in `{{volunteerRole}}`, while `/admin/tasks` carries `volunteerRoleChoicesAgreement`; the stored blanks, the fingerprint and the PDF follow (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given «Dă-i rolul …», when anyone but the Organizer, an Administrator or a Superadministrator asks — the Tehnic role, the Redactor, the desk Volunteer, a member — then the server refuses (`FORBIDDEN`) and nothing is written or sent (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Given a person's offers to volunteer, when «Toate datele unei persoane» is read or exported, then each lists the role given (or none) and every role the person ticked; no public page, cache or event file names a volunteer or their choices (2026-10-14, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
